title: Source collections
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/source-collections, application/json: one part of the complete listing of the collections the adapter can reach through one connection, sent when the connection is made, whenever that set changes, whenever a listed collection's environment_ref changes, comes or goes, and whenever a listed collection's items: false comes or goes. The control plane records each collection's latest environment_ref from the latest listing that contains the collection; a listing that leaves it out means that the collection has no environment definition. The control plane records each collection's grant_ref in the same way, from the latest listing that contains the collection, so the collections of a grant are the collections whose latest grant_ref is that grant's. A grant end ends the collections of that grant (grant-end.schema.json). A listing contains a collection only under a grant that the control plane's copy of grants has under that connection (grants.schema.json): a grant whose report the control plane answered with the signed 204, or that GET /v1/grants or a grant entry, linked, of the change feed shows. While the report of the grant that covers a collection is not accepted, the adapter leaves that collection out of every part of the listing and sends the listing's last part with complete: false, as for a collection whose environment definition it cannot read, so the listing disconnects none of the collections it leaves out. Once the control plane accepts that report, the adapter sends the listing again with the collection. The control plane refuses a part that contains a grant_ref its copy of grants does not have under connection_id, 400 invalid_request, after it decides connection_unknown, connection_ended and connection_suspended. On that refusal the adapter keeps its state, reads GET /v1/grants, and sends the listing again, built anew, without the collections of a grant the copy does not have. The control plane records each collection's items in the same way, from the latest listing that contains the collection: a listing that contains the collection without items means that it has items whenever its source does, and a collection left out of a listing that is not complete keeps its last items value. An adapter that cannot read a collection's environment definition leaves that collection out of every part of the listing and sends the listing's last part with complete: false, so the listing disconnects none of the collections it leaves out, since only a complete listing does, and it changes neither that collection's record nor its environment_ref nor its items. Every part of a listing has the same connection_id. A collection is a place at the source that items are listed from, such as a project, a board or a queue. Collections belong to the connection that listed them, keyed on the adapter, the connection and the collection's ref. A connection is made when the control plane accepts a linked connect return, as described under connection_id in definitions.schema.json; the first listing after that reports its collections, and may be one empty part with complete: true. A collection is not active by being listed: it is linked while it is assigned to a workspace in the control plane and set to have its items come in, and neither it nor its source is listed or described as having no items (items: false); the adapter learns that from the change feed (changes.schema.json). A complete listing, every part from 1 to n arrived and part n with complete: true, disconnects, as sources/disconnect would, every collection of that connection it left out whose last change is older than its started_at, and closes no other connection's collection. A ref is unique among the integration's live collections. A listing that contains a ref live under another connection of the integration ends that collection, as a disconnect would, and creates a new one under this connection; nothing moves between connections. A listing leaves the ref where it is when the other connection's collection has been in a listing of that connection whose started_at is later than this listing's started_at: it ends nothing and creates nothing for that ref, and its part is answered as any accepted part is. The control plane compares the listings' started_at, never the times their parts arrive. An adapter lists only refs the source grants that connection when it reads them, and a grant is linked to at most one live connection (connect-pass.schema.json), so a listing ends another connection's collection only when the source has really moved the collection between grants. Ending the other connection's collection ends that one collection only, never its connection. The end and the new collection are separate changes: when this connection has ended, or its organisation is out of use, by the time the new collection would be created, none is created, and the ref stays ended until a later listing contains it. When the ended collection was linked, the change feed has an unlinked entry for its ref, followed by the new collection's entries once it is linked. The ref refers to one live collection at a time, so the last entry per ref stays its current state. Items and the change feed refer to a collection by its ref alone, sources/disconnect refers to it by its ref and its connection_id, and comments refer to an item by its item_ref; see definitions.schema.json for which collection answers each. The control plane refuses a connection_id that it does not hold for this adapter, 403 connection_unknown, with the same signed body for every cause, and a pending connection is answered 403 connection_unknown on every request but POST /v1/connections/disconnect, which ends it with the signed 204, and POST /v1/sources/disconnect, which is answered with the signed 204 and changes nothing (sources-disconnect.schema.json) (refusal.schema.json); then a connection that ended, 409 connection_ended, final for that connection; then a connection whose organisation is out of use for now, 409 connection_suspended, which is not final: the adapter changes no state and sends the listing again on its periodic check. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. It is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

connection_id.description: The connection the collections are reached through, as it was in its connect pass (connect-pass.schema.json).

collections.description: This part's collections, at most 100. A listing of none, complete, means that the adapter reaches no collection through that connection.

url.description: The collection's page at the source.

title.description: The collection's name at the source.

grant_ref.description: The grant under the same connection that covers the collection: its grant_ref, as the adapter reports it with POST /v1/grants (grant.schema.json).

target.description: Where a change for the collection's items would go. Absent when the adapter names none.

environment_ref.description: The id of the collection's environment definition, as definitions.schema.json describes it. Absent when the collection has none.

items.description: false while the collection has no items, as when the source keeps no items for it. Absent, the collection has items whenever its source does (description.schema.json, roles.source.items). It can change from one listing to the next. While it is false, the control plane treats the collection as a collection of a source that reports no items and does not link it: when the collection was linked, the change feed has an unlinked entry for it, and a linked entry again once a later listing leaves items out while the collection is still assigned to a workspace and set to have its items come in; a POST /v1/source-items for the collection, or a POST /v1/source-items/comments for one of its items, is refused, 409 collection_not_linked (refusal.schema.json). Its environment_ref, its prebuilds and its runs, queued or in progress, are not affected.

listing.description: Which part of which listing this is.
